‘He got the wrong guy’: Kamloops vigilante sentenced for slashing stranger’s tires

Vigilante slashes wrong tires

Tim Petruk - Aug 31, 2026 / 12:28 pm | Story: 629646
Photo: Castanet
FILE - The Kamloops Law Courts
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:28
Instaread

A man who took “vigilante justice” into his own hands by slashing three tires on a car in a Kamloops parking lot, only to discover he targeted the wrong vehicle, has been sentenced to probation.

David Don Repar, 47, was sentenced Thursday in Kamloops provincial court after pleading guilty to mischief under $5,000. He used a knife last summer to puncture tires on a vehicle parked at the Fortune Shopping Centre, 750 Fortune Dr.

Court heard the vehicle’s owner returned to the parking lot on June 25, 2025, to find three of his tires punctured and flattened.

A dashcam captured Repar looking around before approaching the vehicle with what appeared to be a small knife and making stabbing motions toward the tires. The victim paid a $500 insurance deductible to have them replaced.

Defence lawyer Zach Webster said Repar believed he was being harassed by someone who drove an identical vehicle. The owner turned out to be a stranger who had nothing to do with the situation.

“I’m sorry that it happened — it was wrong and I know that,” Repar said in court.

Comparing it to other cases of “vigilante justice," Kamloops provincial court Judge Marian Armstrong rejected Webster’s suggestion the offence was minor. She said Repar acted purposefully, puncturing the victim's tires while looking around to see whether anyone was watching.

“It’s vindictive and wrong,” she said.

Armstrong said Repar should have called Mounties if he believed he was being harassed.

“If Mr. Repar had gone to the police and said, ‘Look, this guy’s harassing me,’ they could have done an investigation — and they would have got the right guy, presumably,” she said.

“But Mr. Repar took it on himself to bring about justice to his harasser, but he didn’t. He got the wrong guy.”

Armstrong sentenced Repar to 12 months of probation, during which time he will be required to complete 15 hours of community service and pay $500 in restitution.

He will also be prohibited from entering or handling someone else’s vehicle unless its owner is present or has given him written permission.
